target_customer: Fashion brands, from first time designers to companies worth over $100M, that need apparel sourced and manufactured
problem: Small fashion brands struggle to find audited factories, manage production and logistics, and avoid delays and mistakes, often through Alibaba or costly sourcing agents.
business_model: Managed sourcing and manufacturing marketplace, earning on production orders

founders.name: Kent Mori
previous_startups: ASPECD (custom fit men's shirts, successful Kickstarter)

founders.name: Shuo Yang
previous_startups: ASPECD (custom fit men's shirts, successful Kickstarter)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says Yang had manufacturing experience that helped ASPECD ship pre-orders.

founders.name: Kevin Chan
previous_startups: ASPECD (custom fit men's shirts, successful Kickstarter)
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder on the YC page and TechCrunch.

exit.reason: Kent Mori published a post dated 2018-09-18 titled 4 Lessons From a Failed Startup that opens by saying Maderight is shutting down. The full text could not be read (403), so the stated cause was not obtained.

competitors.name: Alibaba
competitors.what: Marketplace small brands used to find manufacturers and materials
competitors.traction_then: Commonly used by small brands per TechCrunch, with language and time zone barriers

competitors.name: Maker's Row
competitors.what: Streamlined manufacturer sourcing focused on US factories

competitors.name: Traditional sourcing agents
competitors.what: Intermediaries who arrange factory production, often charging high upfront retainers

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations: vetting factories, production management and a self serve ordering tool. Little novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Audited factory relationships and production experts take time to build, but sourcing agents and marketplaces could be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it as far as sources show. The company shut down in September 2018.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in July 2015 reported over 40 brands signed up since March 2015 and more than 50 audited factories, showing demand from small brands for easier sourcing.

branding.domain_note: maderight.com; a different company called MadeRight (fungi packaging, 2023) shares the name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched ethical, transparent manufacturing with open door factories

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, VentureBeat, TechWeek and Sustainable Brands in 2015. No community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Press about the business, but no evidence of a distinctive brand asset.

outcome_analysis: Maderight grew out of the founders' earlier shirt company ASPECD, where other brands asked for help with production. It left YC and StartX in 2015 with over 40 brands and 50 audited factories and reached 51 people on the YC page. The founders announced a shutdown in September 2018, but the cause was not readable from sources I could open, so it is recorded as not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: maderight.com did not resolve from this session (DNS error), so it is treated as unreachable. The shutdown search result confirmed the Medium post and date from a search summary, but the post body returned 403 and the cause was not obtained. Funding rests on one database (CB Insights, $120K total over 2 rounds, Cherubic Ventures as seed investor, no amount); the $120K is probably YC's standard deal. A $2M MadeRight round in 2023 belongs to a different company. The TechCrunch article says no funding amount. No founder education or prior employers were stated beyond ASPECD.
